title: Summary judgment under Rule 56
summary: Summary judgment decides a claim or defense without trial when there is no genuine dispute of material fact and the movant is entitled to judgment as a matter of law. It examines an evidentiary record rather than only a complaint.
notes: The judge does not weigh credibility or decide among reasonable factual accounts. Necessary discovery and an adequate opportunity to respond matter. The full text of Rule 56 is in the supplement on file (PDF page 90), linked below, and the casebook supplies extensive discussion.

sections.Meaning: Summary judgment decides a claim or defense without trial when there is no genuine dispute of material fact and the movant is entitled to judgment as a matter of law. It examines an evidentiary record rather than only a complaint.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the material elements under substantive law, who bears the trial burden, the movant’s supported showing, and the response. Ask whether a reasonable factfinder could rule for the nonmovant under the applicable evidentiary standard, drawing reasonable inferences in that party’s favor.
